verdict: Progressive earned $2.5B in the quarter as premiums earned rose 5% and underwriting stayed highly profitable — an 88.7% combined ratio, far better than its 96% goal — even though higher claim severity pushed the loss ratio up.

segments.name: Net premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from auto, home and other insurance policies, earned over the coverage period. Personal Lines was $19.1B of it; Commercial Lines $2.8B.

segments.name: Investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the money Progressive invests between collecting premiums and paying claims.

segments.name: Fees and other revenues
segments.note: Policy and service fees collected alongside premiums.

segments.name: Service revenues
segments.note: Revenue from service businesses Progressive runs alongside insurance.

opex.name: Policy acquisition costs
opex.note: Commissions and the cost of winning and writing policies.

opex.name: Other underwriting expenses
opex.note: Running the insurance operations day to day.

opex.name: Service expenses
opex.note: The cost of running Progressive's service businesses.

opex.name: Investment expenses
opex.note: The cost of managing the investment portfolio.

otherDetail: Net realized losses on securities of $170M — $161M of holding-period losses on securities still held and $9M of losses on securities sold.
follow100Note: For every $100 Progressive took in, $10.88 was kept as profit. Revenue here is premiums earned plus investment income, fees and service revenues ($23,362M); reported total revenues were $23,192M after the $170M of realized securities losses shown as other expense. Losses and loss adjustment expenses are an insurer's cost of revenue. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: Underwriting beat its own target by a lot
takeaways.text: The combined ratio of 88.7% means claims and expenses took 89 cents of every premium dollar. Pretax underwriting profit was $2,473M, up from $2,190M — well ahead of Progressive's standing goal of a 96% combined ratio.

takeaways.title: Still growing, just slower
takeaways.text: Policies in force rose 6% year over year (2.4 million more policies) and net premiums written rose 4% to $22.3B. Growth moderated from last year's pace as competition increased and Progressive cut average rates.

takeaways.title: Old claims cost less than expected
takeaways.text: Reserves set aside for prior-year claims proved $534M more than needed, cutting 2.4 points off the combined ratio. Catastrophe losses were $388M, up from $219M a year ago.

oneTimers: No Florida policyholder credits this year: the third quarter of 2025 carried $950M of credits to Florida personal-auto policyholders, which added 4.6 points to last year's underwriting expense ratio — a big reason this year's expense ratio looks so much better.
Net realized losses on securities were $170M, versus gains of $295M a year ago — a $465M swing that explains why net income fell 3% even though underwriting profit rose 13%.
